title: Location Tracking via GPS Data
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted in the data flow can be used to track the child's movements over time, creating a detailed profile of their activities and locations.

title: Identification through Location Patterns
description: Regular GPS transmissions can reveal the child's home, school, and frequent locations, potentially identifying sensitive personal information about their daily routine.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage and Access
description: The backend may store GPS data indefinitely or share it with third parties without proper consent, creating risks of unauthorized access and misuse of location information.

title: Device Impersonation Risk
description: The child's device could potentially be compromised or impersonated, allowing unauthorized parties to transmit false GPS coordinates to the backend.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Location Data
description: Location data stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties, violating user privacy and potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: Location history may be retained longer than necessary for the service, creating ongoing privacy risks and potential for retrospective tracking.

title: Individual Identification from Location Data
description: Stored location data can be used to identify individuals and track their movements, potentially revealing sensitive information about their habits, routines, and associations.

title: User Profiling from Location Data
description: Aggregated location data can be used to create detailed profiles of user behavior, preferences, and patterns, potentially leading to discrimination or targeted manipulation.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The backend may collect more location data than necessary for the service, violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy exposure.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Location data transmitted from P1 to DS1 could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, compromising confidentiality.

title: Location Data Interception in Transit
description: Location pings transmitted between backend and geofencing engine could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling tracking of user movements without consent.

title: Location Data Linkability Across Systems
description: Location data in transit could be correlated with other data sources to build comprehensive movement profiles, enabling cross-system tracking and identification.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Storage
description: Geofencing engine may store location pings beyond processing needs, creating persistent records of user movements that could be accessed without authorization.

title: Inference of User Identity from Location Patterns
description: Geofencing engine could infer user identity or characteristics from location patterns, especially when combined with other available data.

title: Excessive Location Data Sharing
description: Backend may share more location data than necessary for geofencing functionality, increasing privacy exposure and potential for misuse.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of family location zone definitions
description: The Family Account Store shares geofencing zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) that reveal sensitive location information about family members' residences, routines, and social connections. This disclosure could expose private information about where family members live, work, and socialize.

title: Identification of individuals through location zone patterns
description: Zone definitions in transit could be used to identify individuals or their relationships based on location patterns. Knowledge of specific home, school, and social zone locations could enable inference about family composition, daily routines, and social networks.

title: Excessive collection of location data beyond geofencing needs
description: The Geofencing Engine may process more location data than necessary for its intended function. Zone definitions containing detailed location information may be retained or analyzed beyond what is required for basic geofencing alerts, leading to unnecessary data retention.

title: Insufficient user control over location data usage
description: Users may not have adequate control over how their location zone definitions are used by the Geofencing Engine. There may be limited ability to restrict, modify, or delete zone definitions, or to opt out of location-based processing.

title: Location tracking through geofencing notifications
description: The geofencing data reveals when and where a child enters/exits zones, enabling tracking of movement patterns and creating a detailed location history that can be linked to specific times and places.

title: Inference of sensitive location patterns
description: Geofencing data can reveal daily routines, home/work locations, school attendance, and other sensitive behavioral patterns through analysis of entry/exit timestamps and zone associations.

title: Unauthorized interception of location notifications
description: Location notifications transmitted over the data flow could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, exposing movement data to eavesdroppers or malicious actors.

title: Improper storage or sharing of geofencing data by parent entity
description: The parent entity (EE1) may store, process, or share the received geofencing data in ways that violate privacy expectations, such as retaining location history longer than necessary or sharing with third parties.

title: Child Identification Risk
description: The child's profile data (name, DOB, school) is highly identifying and stored at the backend, creating a risk that the child can be identified from the stored data.

title: Data Linkability in Transit
description: Data in transit between parent and backend could be intercepted and linked to identify the child or parent, especially given the sensitive nature of the profile information.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: The backend may store the child's sensitive profile data without adequate access controls, leading to potential unauthorized disclosure to third parties.

title: Parent Identity Usurpation
description: During account registration, the parent's identity could be usurped by an attacker, allowing unauthorized creation of child profiles.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Child data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) is subject to special protections under regulations like COPPA and GDPR-K. The backend may not comply with these requirements.

title: Unauthorized access to stored family account data
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store could be compromised through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access sensitive child profile and geofence zone data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Stored child profile and geofence data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or insider threats, potentially exposing children's personal information and location history.

title: Identification of children through stored profile data
description: Child profile data stored in the Family Account & Permissions Store could be used to directly identify children, potentially exposing their identity, age, and associated family information to unauthorized parties.

title: Linking of child data with external data sources
description: Stored geofence and profile data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, social media, other services) to create detailed behavioral profiles of children, potentially revealing patterns of movement and activities.

title: Insecure data sharing from backend
description: The Mobile App Backend could share data insecurely with the Family Account & Permissions Store, potentially exposing data to interception or unauthorized access during the transfer process.

title: Location data linkage to identify movement patterns
description: Location data transmitted in this flow can be linked across time to identify the child's movement patterns, routines, and locations, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities, school, home, and social interactions.

title: Location data used to identify child's identity
description: Location data in transit can be used to identify the child's identity and whereabouts, especially when combined with other metadata or when the child is identifiable through their device or account.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location data
description: The Mobile App Backend may store or process the child's location data in a way that allows unauthorized access or disclosure to third parties, violating the child's privacy expectations.

title: Parent's monitoring activity reveals sensitive relationship information
description: The parent's act of requesting and sharing location data reveals information about the parent-child relationship and the parent's monitoring behavior, which could be sensitive information about family dynamics.

title: Location Data Interception in Transit
description: Location history data transmitted between datastore and backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing user's movements and identity.

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Location history data in transit could be linked with other data sources to create detailed profiles of user behavior and movements.

title: Sensitive Pattern Revelation
description: Backend processing of location history may reveal sensitive patterns about user's daily routines, frequent locations, and personal habits.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage
description: Backend may store location history beyond necessary retention period or with insufficient access controls, leading to potential unauthorized access.

title: Identification Through Data Sharing
description: The act of sharing location history from the datastore could directly identify the user, especially if combined with other identifying information.

title: Child location data shared with secondary guardian
description: Parent shares child's location data with secondary guardian, potentially exposing the child's movements, routines, and sensitive information about their whereabouts to parties beyond the primary parent

title: Location data in transit can be linked to identify child
description: Location data transmitted between parent and backend could be intercepted and linked to identify the child's movements, potentially revealing patterns of life, school, home, and other sensitive locations

title: Secondary guardian may misuse or further share location data
description: Secondary guardian receiving location data may share it with unauthorized parties, use it inappropriately, or fail to protect the child's privacy expectations

title: Location data enables inference of child's routine and habits
description: Secondary guardian can infer sensitive information about child's daily routine, school attendance, home location, and other patterns from location data, potentially violating child's privacy expectations

title: Identifiability of child's location data
description: The backend shares live location data that can be used to identify the child's movements, home, school, and routine activities, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about the child's life.

title: Linkability of location data to child identity
description: The backend's act of sharing location data may allow the secondary guardian to link location information to the child's identity through metadata or other available information, creating a persistent profile.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data by secondary guardian
description: The secondary guardian may share, store, or disclose the child's live location data to unauthorized third parties, violating the child's privacy expectations.

title: Usurpation of location data access
description: The secondary guardian may misuse the location data for purposes beyond the intended scope, such as tracking the child without consent or using it for surveillance.

title: Identifiability through location metadata
description: Metadata accompanying the location data (such as timestamps, device identifiers, or connection information) may be used to identify the child or link the data to other information sources.

title: Location data interception during transmission
description: Location information sent in the SOS/check-in message could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially revealing the child's whereabouts to third parties.

title: Location data linkability across time
description: The location data can be linked across multiple check-ins to create a movement pattern, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's routine and activities.

title: Child may not fully understand implications of sharing location data
description: The child may not fully understand the privacy implications of sharing their location data, potentially leading to unintended consequences.

title: Parent may use location data beyond intended purpose
description: The parent receiving the location data may use it for purposes beyond the intended check-in/SOS functionality, potentially leading to privacy concerns for the child.

title: Location data could be altered at destination
description: The location data could be tampered with at the destination, potentially leading to false emergency situations or missed emergencies.
